Question: Horses \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) are entered in a three-horse race in which ties are not possible. If the odds against \(X\) winning are \(3\)-to-\(1\) and the odds against \(Y\) winning are \(2\)-to-\(3,\) what are the odds against \(Z\) winning? (By “odds against \(H\) winning are \(p\)-to-\(q\)” we mean that the probability of \(H\) winning the race is \(\frac{q}{p+q}.\))
